Each handshake is between one witch and one sorcerer, since witches don't shake each other's hands and sorcerers don't shake each other's. Each of the 6 witches shakes hands with all 10 sorcerers, giving 6 × 10 = 60 handshakes. Every handshake involves exactly one witch, so none is counted twice.

Solution 1 gives 111. It assumes sorcerer-sorcerer handshakes occurred, which the problem rules out, so its count is wrong.

Solution 2 gives 60, which matches the count above.

Solution 3 gives 30. It wrongly claims that each handshake is counted twice when counting from the witches' side. Since every handshake has exactly one witch, dividing by 2 undercounts.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
